hypothesis: For the seven rules whose SIDE lines put the trade with the quote's step, a trade going against a strong divergence read (the 20-second flow of the newest known dipole event at -0.20 or worse against the trade's side) is entering where the dipole research says a reversal follows, so the decider should skip it.
exact_claim: decider_v1 skips, with the reason tag [divergence], an opening signal of CL01, CL03, CL06, CL10, CL13, CL15 or CL16 (the page says their SIDE lines put the trade with the quote's step) when the 20-second flow carried on the newest dipole event known by then (bought minus sold over bought plus sold) runs against the trade's side at -0.20 or worse. The page rests it on the dipole research in CLAUDE.md (DIVERGENCE: aligned_flow = imb_level x sign(price_drift); strong divergence at or beyond -0.20, about 65% reversal). The page adds that it is the divergence read, not the flow as a direction call.
scope: Opening signals of the seven named rules, on the buy or sell side, when a dipole event is known and bought plus sold is above zero. The page names no trade days and no dates; it says only that the decider was written with 'these trade days' already studied.
boundaries: The -0.20 and the 65 per cent are crypto-era measurements (CLAUDE.md's dipole research, S36); whether they carry to this tape is not shown. The three inferences it needs (flow of the newest event stands for the line now; -0.20 is on the scale of the decider's figure; the seven are the with-the-move rules) are separate files (inference-4a, 4b, 4c). Does not apply to other rules, nor when no dipole event is known. No mirror for entries against the move. Nothing about outcomes is claimed.
mechanism: CLAUDE.md states the crypto-era read: flow aligned with the price drift's sign, at or beyond -0.20, was followed by reversal about 65 per cent of the time. For a rule that trades with the step, the drift's sign is the trade's side, so aligned flow at or beyond -0.20 reads as a trade entered into a probable reversal; the program computes the aligned figure from the packet's 20-second flow fields.
alternatives: The crypto-era figures describe a different instrument and period; on this tape the same threshold may mark nothing.
The program's figure is the 20-second flow, which CLAUDE.md calls the EXHAUSTION line, not the 60-second DIPOLE line; the research's imb_level may be a different quantity from it.
CLAUDE.md's 'Discipline' lines say the signed flow is not a direct direction predictor and that the divergence/flip read is the robust edge; a skip on flow alone may behave as a direction call.
